_note: Written by Claude in a Claude Code session on 2026-11-14, looking at inputs/detail_sample.png. The sample was drawn with faults on purpose, so this is a demonstration, not a blind test.
reviewer: Claude, in a Claude Code session (2026-11-14)

missing: dimensions for parapet height and coping overhang

summary: The parapet is a single uninsulated block wall with a flat coping and a 4 in membrane upturn. Three items would let water in. Three more fail the code or the project mandates.

results.note: Coping drawn flat with no drip.
Upturn labelled 4 in; no termination or counter-flashing.
Nothing drawn between coping and block.
No air or water barrier is drawn on the wall.
Wall insulation stops at the roof slab.
No cleat, blocking, cant or scale.
No reinforcing or bracing shown or referenced; project is seismic design category D.
Same as RP-5: the parapet has no exterior insulation.
No sealant joint is drawn as a water line, so there is nothing to point to.
Same as RP-3: no membrane under the coping.
Parapet height is not dimensioned, so the room for an 8 in base flashing cannot be checked.

findings.title: Membrane upturn is 4 in, not terminated
findings.issue: The roof membrane turns up the parapet only 4 in and ends with no termination bar or counter-flashing. Ponding water or wind-driven rain gets behind it.
findings.recommendation: Carry the base flashing at least 8 in above the finished roof, fasten it with a termination bar and cover it with counter-flashing, or run the membrane up and over the parapet.

findings.title: Coping is flat and has no drip edge
findings.issue: The coping is drawn level and flush with both wall faces. Water sits on it and runs down the cladding and the block.
findings.recommendation: Slope the coping to the roof side, extend it past both faces and add drip edges. Show the continuous cleat.

findings.title: No membrane under the coping
findings.issue: The coping sits directly on open block. Every coping joint is a leak path into the cores of the wall.
findings.recommendation: Add a continuous membrane over sloped wood blocking on top of the parapet, lapped down both faces, before the coping.

findings.title: Parapet is an uninsulated thermal bridge
findings.issue: Exterior insulation stops at the roof slab. The parapet above it is bare block. That breaks project mandate PM-1 (continuous exterior insulation, no uninsulated parapets).
findings.recommendation: Continue the exterior insulation up the outside face to the top of the parapet and insulate the roof side, or add a structural thermal break at the roof line.

findings.title: Air and water barrier not shown across the roof-to-wall line
findings.issue: No wall air barrier is drawn, so there is nothing for the roof membrane to tie into.
findings.recommendation: Draw the wall air and water barrier and show it lapped to the roof membrane over the parapet.

findings.title: Parapet reinforcing or bracing not shown
findings.issue: The block parapet has no reinforcing, bracing or structural reference. The project is in seismic design category D.
findings.recommendation: Show the reinforcing or reference the structural detail for the parapet.

findings.title: No scale, cleat, blocking or cant
findings.issue: The detail has no scale and leaves out the coping cleat, the wood blocking and the cant at the roof edge.
findings.recommendation: Add the scale and tag each item.

control_layers.note: The roof membrane stops 4 in up the parapet. Nothing covers the top of the wall.
No air barrier is drawn on the wall or across the roof line.
Roof insulation and wall insulation do not meet: the parapet between them is bare block.
No vapor control layer is drawn or named.
